chapter_seo_title: Shangjing: Li Huowang Enters the Office’s Lair and Meets a Face-Changer
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang enters Shangjing, the capital of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, witnesses the bizarre “Seize the Bun Mountain” ritual, and violently reacts to a face-changing performer’s stunt.
og_title: Shangjing: A Festival, a Face-Changer, and a Sword at the Throat
og_description: The group arrives in the ancient capital. Bai Lingmiao’s corruption deepens. A harmless opera trick becomes a trigger for Li Huowang’s paranoia.
twitter_title: Li Huowang enters Shangjing and immediately loses it at a face-changing opera performer.
twitter_description: New city, same terror. The buns fly, Bai Lingmiao sasses everyone, and a simple art form becomes an accusation.

lore_anchors.definition: The capital of Great Liang, inherited from the fallen Great Qi Empire; the headquarters of the Supervisory Heavenly Office, and a city built on layers of political and supernatural depth.

A chaotic folk festival where young men scramble to snatch buns from tall towers; the buns are stamped with the longevity character (寿) and the towers are arranged like incense sticks, suggesting a sacrificial undertone.

A traditional Sichuan opera technique where performers rapidly switch between painted masks in the blink of an eye; in this novel, the act triggers Li Huowang’s trauma-driven paranoia due to its resemblance to Zuowandao deception.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body under the imperial board of war; they hunt rogue cultivators and manage supernatural disasters, with their main base in Shangjing.
A high-ranking eunuch official in the Supervisory Heavenly Office; their power is both bureaucratic and supernatural, often wielded through a deceptively genial demeanor.
The modern-world counterpart to the White Jade Capital in the novel's meta-structure; Li Huowang sometimes hallucinates it during transitions between worlds.
